# Performance

### Scope correction: missing QSA is the priority structural issue (2026-10-11)

The current Qwen4Exp graph is a **dense bring-up approximation**, equivalent
to QSA only within its configured selection budget. This is NOT newly
implemented QSA: the earlier documented limitation below (real-prefix scaling
diagnostic) still applies. Extending runtime KV capacity did not add sparse
selection. Previous descriptions of qualified32K model behavior must be read
as same-implementation equivalence/safety/throughput diagnostics, NOT as
original-model long-context correctness. The optimization comparisons remain
valid for the dense implementation; they do not validate its omitted indexer.
This was an important omission in recent promotion/README claims.

Authoritative local evidence: raw config at
`/mnt/noindex/models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4/config.json` has budget2048,
compress_ratio4,index heads4,index dimension128. Original weight index has
`self_attn.indexer.index_qk_proj`,q/k norm tensors in each attention layer.
`models/qwen4_exp.py` rejects graph n_ctx above the budget and calls plain
gated GQA without indexer; runtime capacity expansion bypassed that semantic
scope. Official reference
[Qwen4ExpTextQSAIndexer](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/src/transformers/models/qwen4_exp/modeling_qwen4_exp.py)
pools each four visible raw keys, normalizes/rotates at the first token's
position, ranks blocks with the rectified sum of index-query dot products,
selects512 full blocks and retains the incomplete visible tail. For contiguous
causal history all visible tokens are selected through2051 tokens;2052 is the
first possible drop (2048 conservative graph-budget limit remains valid).

[TensorFold's recipe](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/blob/main/docs/recipes/qwen3.8-flash-next.md)
documents selected-key sparse attention; the
[single-Spark source](https://github.com/MiaAI-Lab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Single-DGX-Spark-TensorFold/blob/main/README.md)
reports prompt measurements spanning8K..128K, not just tiny prompts. Therefore
different input lengths alone cannot dismiss the user's structural concern.
External numbers are source reports, NOT a controlled local same-checkpoint
comparison. Read-only hf-cli model-info resolves current local-inference-lab
Hub revision6c01ac378d22f6652c9f392c87700496eca8e5dc; this does not identify the
revision of already-downloaded local files. No new model download or rewrite.

Added CPU-only `models/qwen4_qsa_reference.py` selection oracle and four
tests: dense-to-sparse transition2051/2052, ranked visible groups/masked gaps,
always-retained tail/32768 history, explicit tie semantics and invalid inputs.
One test demonstrates dense versus QSA output disagreement, rather than
pretending dense baseline equivalence proves correctness. This oracle accepts
precomputed indexer scores: projection/pooling/norm/RoPE/state, selected-key
attention and package integration are **not implemented by this helper**.
Next correctness reference must be the actual QSA model, not old dense logits.

Added `models/qwen4_qsa_indexer_reference.py`: small single-sequence NumPy
FP16/FP32 computation oracle with projection, centered RMSNorm, shared-main-
attention partial RoPE, raw-key cache, visible-group pooling, scoring and
selection. It is **not wired into inference**, does not emulate BF16, and is
not a GPU throughput or original-checkpoint quality result. Six CPU tests
cover scalar arithmetic, independent scalar selection with offset positions,
mask gaps/tails, full versus irregular chunks/one-token decode, reset and
invalid-call state preservation. Per-row FP32 projection reduction is explicit
to keep this oracle independent of BLAS batch-size-dependent reduction order;
this is not a proposed fast runtime projection implementation.

Read-only safetensors HEADER inspection (no payload loaded) confirms 39 indexer
tensors: 12 main-attention layers plus one MTP layer, each BF16 projection
640x2560 and two BF16 norm vectors128. Total42,605,056 bytes, main-only
39,327,744 bytes (~37.5MiB). This establishes the small missing-weight size,
not package integration: a supplementary weight artifact could avoid rewriting
the existing ~123GB package, but no such artifact or runtime loading path has
been implemented yet. CUDA QSA/state and gathered selected-key attention remain
the next implementation work; long-context dense diagnostics remain limited.

### Runtime host-headroom watchdog in real chat/bench entry points (2026-10-11)

added an external sampling guardian. The real Linux chat/bench binaries now

CPU execution do not enable the environment-driven monitor. PPL entry point
is unchanged and still needs its existing external experimental guardian.

Reader is shared with allocation admission and requires a valid MemAvailable
kB value without byte-size overflow. On a below-threshold or unreadable
sample, the CLI logs the reason and `_Exit(137)` ONLY its own process;
no parent/process-group signals, shell background wrapper, GPU reset, driver
change or model-buffer allocation. Emergency shutdown skips GPU synchronization
and model destructors. Since raw-mode REPL line editing may be active while
idle, capture startup stdin termios and attempt restoration before emergency
exit. Normal shutdown wakes/joins the thread. This is best-effort sampling,
NOT reservation, a hard memory limit, bounded peak memory or OOM immunity.

### Logical prefill: independent context capacity and configurable batches (2026-10-09)

Removed the experimental coupling between context capacity and logical batch
size in CLI, PPL, load-time liveness admission, and runtime prefill admission.
`--n-ctx 16384` is now independent of `--prefill-chunk-size`: supported sizes
are1..2048;0 defaults to2048. This retains the qualified per-batch operator
limit rather than extending kernels to arbitrary query counts. Regular
non-logical reclamation keeps its previous limits. No weights/defaults changed.

`prefill()` splits longer inputs into configured chunks and appends KV.
`prefill_hidden()` is a single graph invocation and rejects inputs above its
batch limit. Each actual logical chunk checks an additional4 GiB above the
existing host headroom guard; this is admission, not reserved memory or an
OOM guarantee. Allocation guards and bounded output pool remain active.
Attention head/query grouping retains its <=4096-key predicate; longer KV
uses the existing non-grouped attention path rather than extending optimized
kernel eligibility. Its score scratch can grow with query count times KV length.

Read-only inspection of the calibrated package prefill graph finds no explicit
CONTIGUOUS nodes. CUDA dispatch also launches `contiguous_cuda` for a RESHAPE
whose input is non-contiguous. The builder's comment that reshape inherits
strides is not generally true of the current executor/backend implementation.

New `tools/audit_prefill_outputs.py --layout-copies-only --seq 1743` reads only
the package header and graph, never weight payloads. Under the explicitly
declared unfused dense-producer layout assumption, it reports72 materializing
reshape nodes:36 outputs of6144*1743 FP32 elements and36 of512*1743. This is
consistent with the archived profile's36 launches/grid41832 and36/grid3486
per measured prefill window; grid/count agreement alone is not per-node trace
attribution. These two groups sum13.069332ms and1.067328ms respectively, not
a newly measured model run or a large enough explanation for the full gap.

Of these,48 reshape nodes split the contiguous feature dimension of a padded
2D row view into head_dim/heads, retaining the original token-row stride.
An exact address-preserving split is possible without copying these inputs:
24 large and24 small outputs,1113735168 logical bytes at1743 tokens. This is
declared potential materialization storage, NOT measured DRAM traffic, saved
latency, memory headroom, or throughput improvement. The remaining24 reshapes
merge token/head dimensions after permutation and must not blindly alias.
The audit intentionally keeps current copied layouts for downstream analysis;
it does not propagate the proposed view as though runtime supported it.

CTA/token computes the ordered10-route BF16 sum plus shared branch ONCE in

### Logical full-batch MoE: selection decoupled from window merging (2026-10-09)

CUDA backend now exposes an explicit phase-scoped
`set_logical_prefill_batch(bool)` admission hook. Other backends reject enable
by default; CUDA defaults off and refuses mode changes during its stream
capture. This does NOT change engine chunk/liveness/memory admission and is
not yet called by the full-model prefill entry.

`Nvfp4PrefillBatchPolicy` shares the same bounded row eligibility between a
logical batch and paired-window aggregation. Fused MMA activation accepts
16..2048 rows in either scope, versus the unchanged ordinary 16..1024 scope;
input K-major accepts 1025..2048 only in an explicitly large-batch scope.
All existing resident layout/calibration/alignment/geometry/flag conditions
remain. Compact logits, token quantization and paired token words inherit
that selection; original descriptors and decode paths remain unchanged.
No concat/split tensors are required to enable the new logical-batch scope.

### Safe compact-carry restoration primitive (2026-10-09)

Added `launch_hc_compact_carry_materialize` to the CUDA elementwise library.
It restores known high16 carry bits from the first half of an existing logical
FP32 allocation: ordered D2D copy to caller-owned scratch, then integer decode
into the original allocation. Direct parallel in-place expansion is unsafe
because a CTA could overwrite another CTA's unread packed data. No allocation
or synchronization in this API; caller must retain buffers until completion.
Rows1..1024 (small windows allowed for fallback, NOT a decode selector), max
scratch20MiB. Reject nulls, invalid rows, alignment, insufficient capacity,
address overflow, and scratch overlap with the ENTIRE logical FP32 span before
enqueueing anything. Backend must account for/reserve this scratch separately;
this API alone does not enforce the backend's memory budget.

### Register-decoded W4A16 down projection diagnostic (2026-10-09)

Independent `bench_cuda_nvfp4_w4a16` target only; no backend selector, arena,
model default, package or weight-file changes. BF16 input remains unquantized.
Packed FP4 weights and FP8 block scales are decoded to BF16 pairs in registers,
then accumulated with BF16 m16n8k16 MMA; row/route scales apply at the end.
This is a single ordered K16 accumulation chain, NOT the TensorFold kernel's
per-K16 partial-dot/scaled-FMA chain or pipelined register staging.

Three variants: canonical row/pair gather N8; fixture-prepacked coalesced
M16/K16 register fragments N8; same fragments reused across N16 routes.
Fixture fragment packing preserves code bytes and uses no expanded BF16
weights; temporary small diagnostic allocations are not a proposed duplicate
resident arena. Initial dynamic FP4 lookup generated32 bytes of stack and
was severely slower; independent bit decoding removes it. Final variants use
39/39/45 registers, zero stack/local/shared bytes.

### GDN chunkwise algebra proof: structural direction, not a GPU gain (2026-10-08)

Current CUDA quad-value recurrence and CPU prefill both update the state
sequentially per token. Serialized package audit confirms36 GDN_PREFILL nodes,
all16 key heads/48 value heads (repeat3), key/value dimensions128, flags3
(normalized q/k and sigmoid output gate). Current measured recurrence family
is approximately124ms per1743-token prompt; even eliminating ALL of it would
not alone close the1307 ->2000TPS gap.

Investigated the chunkwise/WY direction described in the primary
[Gated Delta Networks paper](https://jankautz.com/publications/GatedDeltaNet_ICLR25.pdf).
Added independent CPU-only `tools/probe_gdn_chunkwise.py`, deriving the
following matrices from our existing recurrence (state layout is key x value,
transposed relative to the paper). This is NOT a CUDA dispatch or new policy.

For a chunk, P_t is the product of decays through t; Gamma_tj is the direct
product of decays j+1..t for j<=t, otherwise zero. Compute Gamma directly,
NEVER as P_t/P_j: zero decay and FP32 prefix underflow must remain finite.
Let L be the strict lower triangle of diag(beta)*Gamma*(K*K^T), elementwise
where appropriate, and A=(I+L)^-1. Then chunk-local coefficients are
U=A*diag(beta)*V and W=A*diag(beta*P)*K. For incoming state S:

```
H       = U - W*S
O       = [(diag(P)*Q)*S + ((Q*K^T) .* Gamma)*H] * scale
S_next  = P_last*S + (diag(Gamma_last)*K)^T*H
```

U/W and chunk-local dot products are independent of incoming state, so their
preprocessing can be parallel across chunks. State-dependent updates become
55 chunks at C32 (28 at C64) for1743 tokens, instead of1743 per-token updates.
This is a dependency-count reduction, NOT a measured speedup or proof that
coefficient preparation, triangular solve, scratch traffic or Tensor Core
precision is free.

Seven CPU algebra tests cover C1/16/32/64/128, rectangular head dimensions,
ragged tails, changed initial states, no input mutation, correlated keys,
beta0/1, decay0/1/1e-4, prefix underflow,1024+719 carried windows, repeat3
independent value-head gates/state, and invalid shapes/values/precisions.
FP64 checks use absolute1e-11, FP32 synthetic checks1e-5; these are algebra
checks against the CPU mathematical recurrence, NOT tolerances for accepting
a model regression or emulation of CUDA warp/FMA reduction. All comparisons
retain full output and final state, not just aggregate loss. Separate1743/
128x128 probes C16/32/64/128 all pass eight dtype/fixture records each.
FP32 results are explicitly NOT byte-exact; production/model quality gates
are unchanged. Evidence `gdn-chunkwise-math{16,32,64,128}.log` and
`gdn-chunkwise-math-test-final.log`.

(`gdn-chunkwise-math-{register-build,focused}.log`). No CUDA kernel, backend,

Source inspection also identifies a frame-isolation requirement:
`CudaBackend::upload_input` reuses `boundary_buffers[key]`, and engine
`run_graph` passes names such as `hidden`, `mask`, `cos` and `sin` as keys.
Concurrent suspended frames cannot upload under those same keys: the second
frame can overwrite/reallocate the first frame's storage. Future integration
must allocate private frame boundary tensors (as this test does) or explicit
bounded namespaced slots; simply cloning the graph/ExecContext is insufficient.
HC projection plans are indexed per Graph, while activation/half-shadow epoch
is global; segment begin invalidation prevents trusting another frame's epoch.

### Bounded scheduling prerequisite: resumable unfused graph segments (2026-10-08)

Added `execute_graph_segment(ctx, first, end)` for exclusive-end, consecutive
node-index ranges. Only the first segment resets intermediate tensors and
initial prefetch; resumed segments retain live materialized owners and borrowed
views. Existing last-use queues continue reclaiming storage inside each range.

caches rather than trust another frame's activation/HC epoch. Dynamic workspace
shape validity is published only after the last segment. Ordinary full execution
remains the production path and explicitly abandons any suspension.

not an input snapshot: callers must keep inputs and graph runtime storage stable

### HC up/reduce CUDA opt-in: bounded model gain (2026-10-08)

Added default-off `MOLLM_CUDA_HC_PREFILL_UP_REDUCE_FUSION=1`. Requires existing
sigmoid/reduce fusion and deferred-RMS support; FP32 reference mode and capture
retain the original path. Concrete dispatch checks FP32 contiguous normalized/
low-rank/output shapes10240/320/2560,rows16..1024, up10240x320 supported Q4G32
or FP16 weight, activation parameters and fresh deferred owner/reduce pointer/
epoch/row count/unreduced state. Rejects graph-output/input/carry/gamma/inverse
overlap. Converts low-rank input to FP16, reuses the existing FP16 cache or
existing Q4G32 expansion kernels, checks prepared operand alignment/alias and
writes the reduction output directly. No persistent weight representation or
package conversion changes. Successful enqueue marks the deferred owner
reduced; CUDA errors fail execution, unsupported configuration reconstructs

### Down-path cache/latency counters after structural audit (2026-10-08)

Two independent Nsight Compute processes profile exactly one current
`nvfp4_native_batched8_mma_cuda<1,1,0,0,1>` launch each, with four warps,
canonical pair layout, prequantized input and BF16 output. Existing bounded
`bench_cuda_nvfp4_bf16_output --rows 1024 --counts ...` replays node164's
512-expert route histogram (10240 jobs); weights/inputs are synthetic.
Grid40x10240,128 threads, source-matched model down2560/K640/N8. This is
NOT a whole-model profile, nor newly traced routing under latest flags.
No inference source/build changes. Root collector only, clock-control none,
cache-control none, no kernel/model sanitizer, reset or driver changes.

| Counter | First | Independent repeat |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Instrumented kernel duration ms | 2.309664 | 2.320608 |
| L1 sector hit % | 64.72 | 64.54 |
| L2 aggregate sector hit % | 75.21 | 75.22 |
| L2 read sectors | 47904869 | 47912232 |
| L2 read lookup-hit sectors | 35919926 | 35920820 |
| L2 read lookup-miss sectors | 11325336 | 11330312 |
| L2 throughput % of sustained peak | 30.85 | 30.72 |
| Tensor-pipe active cycles % of elapsed | 3.39 | 3.40 |
| SM throughput % of sustained peak | 18.62 | 18.69 |
| Long-scoreboard stalls per active warp % | 80.35 | 90.27 |

Device metric discovery exposes NO `dram__bytes_read.sum`,
`dram__bytes_write.sum` or `dram__throughput.avg.pct_of_peak_sustained_elapsed`.
Thus this experiment cannot establish DRAM bandwidth/saturation. Read hit
plus miss counters do not sum to total reads; do not treat them as an exact
partition, derive missing traffic, or convert sectors into total DRAM bytes.
Aggregate hit percentage includes other accesses. Uncontrolled caches/clocks
and replay prevent using these instrumented durations as a TPS comparison.
Long-scoreboard percentage varies substantially even though the other
counters repeat closely. Tensor active cycles are not % of peak useful FLOPs.

Confirmed source distinction: gateN32 stages canonical weights asynchronously
in shared memory; downN8 reads weight codes/scales and packed input fragments
directly from global memory inside its K64 loop, with no corresponding
operand-staging pipeline. Counter evidence supports testing latency hiding
and operand reuse on this down path, not concluding that NVFP4 MMA arithmetic
or DRAM bandwidth is itself the limiting resource. Wider-down experiments
already showed that simply changing N8 to N16 is not a sufficient answer.
1480 actual N8 batches imply59200 useful CTAs in this fixture versus409600
allocated; sparse early-return CTAs can affect aggregate activity. This does
not quantify their time or establish compact dispatch would be faster.

combine checks across layouts,20 projection rejects,13 combine rejects and48
route-pointer cases. No model quality or new speedup claim. Two valid-run
guardians95 samples/min120220368KiB, no stop; nvidia-smi has no compute
application afterward. Kernel journal checked over the measurement interval,
no matching NVRM/Xid/OOM. No headroom/chunk/context changes.

### Structural prefill audit: route-batch payload accounting (2026-10-08)

User-requested shift from instruction tuning to execution/dataflow diagnosis.
Added optional `--qwen38-nvfp4-dataflow` to the existing validated route trace
analyzer. No inference dispatch, kernel, checkpoint, cache, chunk or context
change. The mode requires48 layers/512 experts/top-k10. Uses the historical
96-record trace `build_cuda/qwen38-stateful-contract-route-counts1024.log`
(1024+719 rows), NOT a newly collected trace under vector quantization.
Current source confirms hidden2560/inter640, gateN32/downN8, K16 NVFP4,
two expert-dependent gate/up input globals, BF16 gate/down intermediates and
packed-only activation in the retained opt-in configuration.

Each expert route batch traverses a complete projection tiled over output
rows. Count its UNIQUE FP4 codes and K16 scales once per batch: this is a
logical payload model, NOT instruction load bytes, cache misses, measured
DRAM bandwidth, allocated memory or a speedup prediction. Excludes row
globals, descriptors, duplicate lane reads and transaction amplification.
An active expert once per chunk is a comparison baseline, not a realizable
zero-cost algorithm or a lower bound on actual hardware transactions.

| Chunk rows | Gate routes/traversal | Down routes/traversal | Gate payload GB | Down payload GB | Active-expert once GB |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1024 | 19.0209 | 7.0569 | 47.6301 | 64.1904 | 43.6755 |
| 719 | 16.1098 | 6.7317 | 39.4869 | 47.2486 | 42.6636 |

Decimal GB, whole prompt gate/down batch payload198.5559552GB versus
86.3391744GB active-once comparison. Vector gate quantizer source requests
17.1343872GB (top-k10 x two variants, source values read once/variant),
packed/scales writes2.4095232GB. BF16 gate writes2.1417984GB, packed-only
activation writes0.3011904GB, BF16 down writes4.2835968GB. These separate
pass-boundary counts exclude subsequent reads and are not total traffic.
Top-k source rows share values but expert-dependent calibrated globals mean
their FP4 codes/scales cannot generally be shared unchanged.

Interpretation: inspect cross-route weight reuse and intermediate-memory
traffic before further barrier/instruction tuning. Do NOT conclude DRAM is
the bottleneck from these numbers: L2 can absorb repeated payloads, and
earlier wider-down probes did not establish a material model benefit.
Likewise N32 route-slot fill59.44%/50.34% is not tensor-core occupancy.
The previous whole-model profile predates parallel-plan/vector-quant changes;
its97.863% kernel interval coverage excludes dominant launch-idle time in
that window but does not establish GPU saturation or current family costs.
Next discriminating measurement is bounded selected-kernel cache/DRAM and
effective math utilization, then a source-compatible reuse redesign; no
large-chunk retry is justified by this offline audit.

Reproduce:

```sh
python3 tools/analyze_cuda_prefill_routes.py \
  build_cuda/qwen38-stateful-contract-route-counts1024.log \
  --chunk-rows 1024,719 --layers 48 --qwen38-nvfp4-dataflow
```

### Diagnostic output-pool cache reclamation primitive

Added `trim_free_device_buffers(pool, stream, reclaimed_bytes)` to CUDA device
runtime, deliberately NOT called by inference. Frees only blocks already
returned to the pool; removes freed addresses from allocation/size ownership
records, preserves active allocations, and reports actual reclaimed bytes.
Rejects capture on the supplied stream before freeing anything. Caller must
also exclude other-stream capture and invalidate cached graphs referring to
cached blocks before use; being in the freelist alone does not prove absence
of cached CUDA Graph references. No headroom reduction, automatic retry,
default/runtime selector or model-safe reclamation claim.

### Opt-in CUDA output-pool reservation limit

`MOLLM_CUDA_OUTPUT_POOL_MB` (MiB, default unset/0=disabled) is parsed once per
backend. Non-digit/sign/space/overflow values reject backend initialization.
Before a NEW output allocation would exceed the configured pool reservation
limit, the backend calls the validated cache-invalidation/reclaim path; then
rechecks actual reserved bytes with overflow-safe subtraction. Best-fit reuse
requires no new allocation/reclaim. A request itself above the limit rejects
immediately; active storage preventing fit also rejects, without freeing active
buffers. Capture/pending-replay refusal stops allocation rather than freeing
referenced storage. Original host-headroom guard still applies to new CUDA
allocations; no change to its margin, no CUDA-OOM retry or CPU fallback added.

This option bounds output pool only, NOT weights, recurrent/KV state, state
snapshots, scratch, library/driver allocation or whole-host pressure. Reclaim
adds synchronization/capture rebuild costs; no stable model throughput gain
or system-wide OOM guarantee. Weight/package layouts/default chunk unchanged.

### Diagnostic pedantic-FP32 GEMM attention: about2x operator speedup (2026-10-06)

Added diagnostic-only `launch_sdpa_prefill_fp32_gemm`. It expands the active
FP16 KV cache into two caller-owned FP32 buffers with exact half-to-float
conversion, computes QK with per-head `cublasGemmEx` using
`CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F_PEDANTIC`, applies scale/explicit-mask-or-implicit-causal
mask plus FP32 softmax, then computes PV with the same pedantic FP32 mode.
No TF32, new activation quantization or model-weight/layout changes. Float
accumulation order differs from the original SIMT kernel, so it is NOT an
exact-numerics replacement. No production backend selector or integration.

Caller supplies disjoint scores H*Q*K and two scratch buffers KVH*K*D floats;
feature strides are one, cache is head-position-feature, query/output have
arbitrary supported leading/head strides. Existing cuBLAS handle must use
host scalar-pointer mode and the explicit stream; the launcher checks this
without modifying handle state. Parameter/grid/size overflow checks precede
work; execution failure is returned as status, not a safe fallback after
partial launches. The first prototype issues two GEMMs per head, rather
than one batched call, leaving a concrete further optimization opportunity.

`bench_cuda_sdpa_prefill --gemm` passes50 fixtures with three changed-Q/K/V/
mask captured replays, comparing finite logical outputs against the original
SIMT kernel within `2e-5*(1+abs(reference))`. Actual maximum absolute error
is3.27826e-7. Padding/guard entries remain byte-identical. Cases cover
dimensions128/256, past KV, keys3/7/129/857/1024/1025, padded query/output/cache
strides, explicit masks (biases plus -infinity and finite -1e38) and implicit
causal/noncausal behavior. Fourteen invalid argument/stride/stream/pointer-
mode cases reject without kernel launches. This is an operator comparison,
not an independent CPU mathematical reference or model-quality result.
The unchanged legacy diagnostic additionally passes its49 exact comparisons.

### Prepared canonical MMA fixed-step fragment addressing: numerical gate (2026-10-06)

The optional prepared N8/N16 implementation now resolves canonical row/pair
weight base addresses before the K64 loop. Subsequent tiles advance128 bytes
in pair layout or32 bytes in row layout; second K32 fragment is64/16 bytes
ahead respectively, and row r+8 is4*K bytes ahead in either layout. Block

### Stable radix grouping implementation and correctness (2026-10-06)

Added default-off `MOLLM_CUDA_NVFP4_PREFILL_RADIX_GROUP=1` for resident
multirow prefill candidates. Replaces quadratic pointer ranking with CUB
stable radix sort of full unsigned weight addresses and original-slot indices,
followed by a descriptor scatter. Both gate/down output/input pointers, scaling
metadata and equal-key original ordering remain unchanged. This API does not
generate the optional legacy SIMT pair plan; existing paired grouping remains
untouched. No package/weight-layout changes or new model conversion.

no allocations or synchronization inside the launcher. Rejects undersized or
misaligned scratch, overlapping output ranges, output/input overlap and scratch/
descriptor overlap. Read-only input ranges may overlap. Count0 is a no-op,
counts outside0..65535 reject. Backend radix flag also permits grouping above
4096 routes without the tiled flag, while default-off and single-row decode
retain old selection. Scratch is separate from MMA scratch and freed normally.

ordinary duplicates, high pointer bits including the unsigned top bit, and all
equal/null keys. Checks every descriptor field, including signed-zero scale
bits and both input/output pointers, rather than just sorted keys. Legacy and
tiled paired/unpaired cases remain covered; radix is tested unpaired only.

### Split compact dispatch avoids regression, only marginal prefill gain (2026-10-06)

Current compact implementation uses a single-batch main grid and a separately
launched persistent overflow grid. Host grid size is merely a performance hint;
device-side batch count and overflow handling preserve all work even if the
hint is too small. Backend hints ceil(routes/8)+ceil(7*experts/8), capped at
routes. Builder reserves each equal-expert run's entire compact range with one
atomic, preventing interleaved batches of different experts. Within each run,
batch boundaries and route/output positions remain unchanged. Expert-run order
may differ, but per-route arithmetic and later route reduction order do not.

Prepared canonical main kernel uses64 registers, same as old sparse dispatch;
overflow uses72, shared1024B, no local spills. Both register-control changes
and contiguous run reservation differ from the negative loop experiment, so
the improvement over that experiment cannot be attributed to one change alone.
CUDA-device fixture runs at2/4/8 batch warps all pass bit-exact comparisons,
including ragged tail warps with repeated overflow iterations and changed-input/
metadata captured replays. All current31 CUDA regressions pass32.50s.

### Decode host-API overlap audit (2026-10-06)

`tools/analyze_cuda_decode_profile.py --runtime-api` clips runtime events
to the same head-bounded final decode window and intersects each with the
merged kernel interval union. Host API duration includes waiting for queued
GPU work; neither total API time nor its no-kernel portion proves causal
overhead. API sums can overlap across host threads. Eleven offline tests
pass, including clipped API intervals, outside-window exclusion and missing
runtime-table rejection.

Existing register-state node capture, final31-token window775.423ms:
342 synchronous memcpy calls occupy688.544ms host time, of which671.176ms
overlaps kernels;17.368ms does not. Graph launch45.474ms overlaps43.110ms;
device synchronize12.973ms overlaps11.558ms. The kernel union remains
750.298ms (96.760% of the window), not device utilization. A separate
copy-event direction/size audit attributes664.576ms of memcpy host duration
to30 eight-byte D2H result copies (actual transfer intervals total0.046ms).
These occur at token completion; they are not PLE table transfers. The final
head-bounded window excludes the final argmax readback, hence30 not31.
Do not infer hundreds of milliseconds of removable transfer overhead or
an async-copy speedup from the host API totals. This is an instrumented
existing trace, not a new uninstrumented throughput benchmark.
Evidence: `build_cuda/qwen38-current-runtime-overlap-audit.log`, derived
from `build_cuda/qwen38-gdn-register-state-nodes.sqlite`.

### Direct E4M3 FP32 scale construction rejected (2026-10-06)

Diagnostic `launch_nvfp4_pipelined_projections(..., direct_scale=true)`
constructs normal E4M3 values as exact FP32 exponent/mantissa/sign bits,
uses exact power-of-two scaling for subnormals, and retains hardware decode
for NaN. A separate GPU fixture compares all 256 raw-code FP32 bit patterns
against the existing FP8-to-half-to-float path; all match, including signed
zeros and NaNs. The ordinary inference specialization stays unchanged.

With canonical pair-layout actual expert shapes, gate1280/K2560 takes
92.430–92.591 us vs 83.950–84.926 us; down2560/K640 takes
53.112–53.596 us vs 45.346–46.096 us. All rotating sets, final timed graph
outputs and changed-input replays of the same candidate graph match SIMT
bitwise. No runtime selector was added and no model gain is claimed.
Evidence: `build_cuda/nvfp4-direct-scale-probe.log`.

### NVFP4 aligned-packet specialization rejected (2026-10-06)

Diagnostic `launch_nvfp4_pipelined_projections(..., aligned_packets=true)`
requires caller-guaranteed two-byte weight and 16-byte input alignment for
every job. It removes packet-level alignment tests, retaining original FP4
decode, scale/FMA order, depth-one full-input pipeline and warp reduction.
It rejects combinations with other diagnostic selectors. Normal inference
uses the unchanged safe alignment fallback; no runtime selector was added.

The actual pair-layout gate (1280-by-2560) takes 85.473–86.103 us vs
83.965–84.749 us for the existing pipeline; down (2560-by-640) takes
47.390–48.079 us vs 45.178–46.634 us. Row-layout candidates also lose.
All rotating weight sets, final timed graph output, and two changed-input
replays of the same candidate graph match the original SIMT path bitwise.
The first probe's changed-input mode erroneously selected row-reuse; this
was corrected before the authoritative checked probe quoted here. Removing
source branches is not sufficient to improve this kernel; the test does not
establish a specific scheduler/register cause. No model gain is claimed.
All 22 CUDA backend regressions pass (21.42 s), separate from diagnostic
graph coverage. Evidence:
`build_cuda/nvfp4-aligned-packets-checked-probe.log`;
`build_cuda/nvfp4-aligned-packets-regression.log`.

### Lossless dense scale palette feasibility audit (2026-10-06)

`MOLLM_CUDA_Q4_PALETTE_AUDIT` reports distinct BF16 scale codes during
existing exact compact W4 conversion, without changing device weights or
the package. The calibrated Qwen3.8 resident + offload-PLE startup audited
48 matrices (N=13312/16480, K=2560): each contained 658–1416 distinct codes.
Therefore a single 256-entry palette per matrix cannot represent these
weights losslessly. No 8-bit palette kernel or runtime compression was
enabled; a segmented dictionary would require separate feasibility and
performance evidence. Log: `build_cuda/qwen38-q4-palette-audit.log`.

| Eight-row banks per segment | Largest dictionary | Segments exceeding 256 codes | Indexed / original bytes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 418 | 6962 | 0.981040 |
| 4 | 737 | 19358 | 0.957511 |
| 16 | 931 | 5882 | 0.948669 |

The hypothetical footprint includes variable-length BF16 dictionaries and
eight one-byte indices per block, but excludes metadata, alignment, and
fallback handling for dictionaries exceeding 256 entries. Thus even the
ratios above are not realizable by a uniform byte-index decoder. No runtime
palette conversion was added. Evidence:
`build_cuda/qwen38-q4-segment-palette-audit.log`;
build: `build_cuda/q4-segment-palette-build.log`.

### Bounded FP16 dense prefill weight cache prototype (2026-10-06)

`MOLLM_CUDA_PREFILL_FP16_CACHE_MB` optionally bounds an expanded FP16 cache
for uploaded immutable Q4G32 dense weights with output width>4096. Default0;
valid budgets0–32768MiB. Both biased canonical and compact layouts use their
existing expansion kernel once during weight upload, outside CUDA capture.
Prefill then converts only activations and uses the same FP16 cuBLAS path;
decode retains the quantized private weight. Cached allocations share the
backend-owned weight lifetime and are freed through device_allocations after
graph teardown. This deliberately spends additional memory, unlike expert
batching; no expert duplicate or package change is introduced. Cache-full
weights retain the existing per-call scratch expansion path.

### Recurrent prefix recovery experiment (2026-10-06)

Default-OFF `MOLLM_CUDA_MTP_STATE_PREFIXES=1` is a candidate to avoid
replaying accepted inputs after a rejected draft. Shortconv and serial GDN
store complete post-token histories/state; pooled device buffers are registered
for every recurrent state. Recovery validates complete coverage and unchanged
spans/addresses before copying anything. Missing coverage falls back to the
original checkpoint plus replay. Retained target hidden and cache lengths are
trimmed to the accepted prefix, not the full rejected verification batch.
CPU/other backends keep default no-op hooks. Temporary prefix addresses never
enter persistent CUDA decode-segment graphs. No model-weight format change.

72 shortconv fixtures cover groups7/257, M2/3/4/5/7/8, kernels2/4/8 and
real-token padding. 96 GDN fixtures cover M2/3/4/5/7/8, padded/unpadded,
four normalization/gating flag combinations and grouped value heads.
Every prefix, output and final state matches independent per-token execution
bitwise; GDN additionally passes same-graph replay with changed QKV and
device-prefix restore followed by the next token.
Saving every prefix costs additional state traffic and multiple state-sized
buffers; the kernel checks alone do not establish a net performance gain.

was not supported, so replay remained5 tokens. OFF41.14/41.33/41.26 vs
ON41.18/41.50/41.53 is not evidence of prefix-recovery acceleration.

with EOS pass interface checks against CPU references; all5 focused CUDA

(+11.25%). Replay5→0 tokens; rollback~98→3.70ms. All three full arrays match

### BF16 MMA split-K scheduling diagnostic (2026-10-06)

Add `MOLLM_NVFP4_BF16_SPLIT_K=1 MOLLM_NVFP4_BF16_BLOCK_WEIGHTS=1` to the

selected rotating set. Maximum normalized error across synthetic fixtures is

### HC unequal W4 projections: kernel baseline (2026-10-06)

`MOLLM_Q4_UNEQUAL_PROBE=1 build_cuda/bench_cuda_projections 320 10240`
tests one launch for the HC lowrank down projection (N320) and injection
projection (N4), which share the normalized K10240 input. Each CTA selects
its independent canonical weight/output pointer and executes the depth1
input-lookahead reduction. There is no weight concatenation, package change,
new exported graph op. This standalone probe excludes runtime delayed-copy
overhead; the opt-in runtime integration above is measured separately.

The control already uses depth1 lookahead for N320, plus the original N4
dispatch. Independent consecutive matrices are assigned to 32 rotating
pairs; approximately128 MiB is allocated, but only approximately64 MiB is
read by the two projections, still above the GB10's24 MiB L2. All pairs
are checked bit-exact before timing. Ordinary launches initially measure
21.68/17.87/17.90 us versus24.81/22.53/22.61 (first sample variable).

Explicit nonblocking-stream graph capture then measures per projection pair
16.73/16.35/16.35 us versus20.59/20.57/19.66. A separate process, alternating
candidate/control measurement order, gives16.45/16.44/17.28 versus
20.62/20.62/19.73. Graphs capture at least one complete rotating-pair pool,
warm up twice and time four replays with CUDA events. These are synthetic
operator results (approximately12–20% lower time), not model tok/s gains.
Five backend regression configurations pass, including graph capture and
two changed-input replays, unequal output guards and invalid arguments.

The two MATMUL nodes are separated by
scalar/SiLU/up/sigmoid/GR-reduce nodes in existing packages. Simply computing
the injection early into a future tensor's pooled allocation is unsafe:
its storage lifetime must be explicitly reserved and graph dependencies
preserved. The runtime integration above therefore explicitly reserves
independent slots rather than writing future reusable pool storage. Existing
packages and other backends are unchanged.
Logs: `build_cuda/q4-hc-unequal-320-4{,-graph,-graph-repeat}.log`.

and runtime weight layout are unchanged.

### Narrow W4 counter audit (2026-10-06)

The dominant N2560/K6144 row projection was profiled separately with Nsight
Compute2026.1.1, kernel-name filter `q4_g32_row_parallel_gemv_cuda`,
launch-skip32/launch-count1, rotating13-set synthetic weights. This is a
matching operator shape, not a complete-model capture. The backend prepares
canonical dense W4 through `Impl::upload_weight`: `cudaMalloc` + H2D copy +
one-time private nibble bias. The mmap-backed package log does not imply that
these hot W4 kernels read file-mapped CPU weights directly.

The ordinary-user attempt fails with ERR_NVGPUCTRPERM. Its extremely distorted
benchmark timings must not be used as performance evidence. Profiling via
`sudo -n` succeeds without changing global profiling permissions. Full section
collection (16 replays) gives physically inconsistent occupancy:277.69% with
clock-control/cache-control none,145.67% with base clocks/all-cache flushing.
The first also reports100.36% L2 hit rate. These broad-section reports cannot
establish achieved occupancy or a whole-model speedup; the cause of their
counter inconsistency is not proven.

A reduced raw-counter capture is one replay, with base clocks and all-cache
flushing. Its counters agree across SM and SMSP domains:
SM cycles elapsed avg231678, active avg224709.979167, warp-active avg
10481648.958333, device limit48 warps/SM. This gives94.254822% elapsed
occupancy and97.177565% active occupancy. Reported SMSP elapsed occupancy
is94.182054%. The standalone narrow kernel therefore does not lack resident
warps in this capture. It does not prove the same percentages for every
real-model launch or under warm, unrestricted-clock conditions.

Stall collection requires separate hardware passes even for selected raw
counters. The three-pass capture reports warp-active517622805,
long-scoreboard396671463 and barrier62402075 (approximately76.63% and12.06%
of warp-active samples). Both ratios are physically plausible, but are not
single-pass-correlated measurements and must not be treated as precise time
savings. Combined with the occupancy check, they motivate investigating
weight/scale/input load dependencies rather than adding more resident warps or
assuming reduction barriers alone are the principal cost. Earlier one-barrier
model A/B already failed to improve throughput.

Reproduction: use `ncu --metrics` to request
`sm__cycles_elapsed.avg,sm__cycles_active.avg,sm__warps_active.avg,`
`smsp__cycles_elapsed.avg,smsp__cycles_active.avg,smsp__warps_active.avg,`
`smsp__warps_active.avg.pct_of_peak_sustained_elapsed,`
`sm__warps_active.avg.pct_of_peak_sustained_elapsed,gpu__time_duration.sum`.
Export `--page raw --csv`; inspect `profiler__replayer_passes` and device limits
before using ratios. The current metric catalog spells stall counters
`smsp__warps_issue_stalled_*`, not `smsp__warp_issue_stalled_*`; unsupported
spellings produce n/a, not usable zeros.
Evidence: `build_cuda/q4-narrow-raw-metrics.{ncu-rep,csv}` (one replay),
`build_cuda/q4-narrow-stall-singlepass.{ncu-rep,csv}` (despite its filename,
THREE replays), and invalid full-section logs
`build_cuda/q4-narrow-{root,controlled}-details.log`.
No production kernel, default option or weight file changed in this audit.

for these shapes; they do not by themselves establish a hardware-counter cause.

### Pooled device recurrent snapshots (2026-10-06)

Default-OFF `MOLLM_CUDA_MTP_DEVICE_CHECKPOINT=1` selects optional
backend-owned immutable recurrent snapshots. Only plain state spans are
eligible: CUDA collections containing host-mirrored/host-authoritative
metadata or a host-only buffer fall back as a whole to the existing transfer
hooks. CPU and other backends remain unchanged. Snapshot creation failure
invalidates the checkpoint instead of silently switching paths; destination
spans and addresses are all validated before restore writes. KV lengths are
still rewound separately, and accepted-prefix replay is unchanged.

Each live snapshot has its own pool lease. Pool ownership is shared so snapshot
destruction remains safe after backend destruction; storage is returned for
subsequent steps rather than repeatedly cudaMalloc/cudaFree'd. The actual
Qwen smoke needs approximately118 MB for a live snapshot, retained in the
pool until its final owner releases it. This is recurrent state, not another
expert/weight copy. Multiple simultaneously live snapshots use distinct leases.
Capture/restore finish their copies before returning; reported timings include
completion, not just asynchronous enqueue time.

First non-pooled attempt regressed to12.17/12.25 tok/s, capture28.38/28.05 ms.
Pooling gives13.41/13.44 versus fresh host-snapshot control12.58/12.82
(approximately5.7% faster), under the exact-W4-reuse/serial-GDN/exact-SDPA
configuration, same dummy16 prompt/8 outputs, warmup1/repeat2.
Capture25.33/20.20→6.21/5.97 ms; rollback155.92/154.79→143.98/146.07 ms.
Both retain1/12 acceptance,6 steps/18 verified tokens and unchanged greedy
IDs220,15,24,24,17,11,24,24. Device-snapshot byte counter equals the total
590,192,700 bytes in both pooled runs (host control device counter is0), proving
the actual model uses the new path rather than a silent host fallback.

Unit coverage includes immutable concurrent snapshots, offset views, duplicate
state pointers, all-span validation before the first write, changed addresses,
wrong-backend restore and mixed-metadata host fallback. Synthetic recurrent
MTP tests require the device byte counter when enabled and compare retained
input replay, logits and subsequent hidden state; CUDA/CPU hidden error is0.
These are fixture checks, not broad quality validation. This dummy-token smoke
remains much slower than serial; see the real-prompt comparison above for higher
acceptance and closer throughput. Keep MTP experimental.
Evidence: `build_cuda/qwen38-mtp-device-checkpoint-pooled.log`,
`build_cuda/qwen38-mtp-device-checkpoint-host-control.log`,
`test_recurrent_checkpoint_device` and `test_recurrent_mtp_device_e2e`.

### Verification arithmetic isolation (2026-10-06)

The actual target probe now has an optional `--strict` mode and an additional
four-position serial-versus-batch comparison. Default remains diagnostic;
strict mode rejects any nonzero hidden/logit difference in its fixture.
`MOLLM_DUMP_NODES=1 MOLLM_DUMP_FIRST_ROW=1` reports first-token signatures
for short executions, accounting for ShortConv's special dim-major physical
output. It omits noncontiguous views and does not cover other outer slices.
This instrumentation synchronizes/copies tensors and must not be used in timings.

An apparent ShortConv mismatch was a diagnostic-layout error, NOT a kernel
bug: both ShortConv and GDN use dim-major QKV, unlike the token-major gate
projections. The attempted cross-backend output-layout change was reverted;
CPU/CUDA/Metal ShortConv arithmetic and physical layouts remain unchanged.
Their stale layout comments are corrected, and the CPU fixture independently
checks batch output/final state against concatenated one-token execution.

With exact W4 and serial short-batch GDN, the first small floating-point
differences arise at SDPA and later amplify through the graph. New default-OFF
`MOLLM_CUDA_SDPA_SMALL_BATCH_EXACT=1` uses decode score/softmax/value
reductions for each query of cached causal batches2..8. Each query only reads
its own prefix even though the cache append is batched; other attention modes
and longer prompt prefill retain their original dispatch.

Combining this switch with `MOLLM_CUDA_Q4_SMALL_BATCH_EXACT=1` and
`MOLLM_CUDA_GDN_SMALL_BATCH_SERIAL=1` gives exact first-position hidden and
logit equality in the actual Qwen fixture, including changed later inputs.

220,15,24,24,17,11,24,24 in both repeats. However throughput is only
11.23/11.19 tok/s, acceptance1/12=8.3%, verify381.88/384.75 ms,
rollback159.37/160.88 ms, versus serial approximately37 tok/s.
This is a diagnostic consistency reference, not a performance win, a broad
quality validation, or grounds to default-enable MTP. The stronger
`--strict` probe also passes all four hidden/logit positions bit-exactly,
not just the first position (`build_cuda/qwen38-verify-all-positions-strict.log`).
Weight files and
package formats are unchanged. Evidence: `build_cuda/qwen38-verify-all-decode-arithmetic.log`
and `build_cuda/qwen38-mtp-all-decode-arithmetic.log`.

All new switches below are default OFF; weight/package layouts are unchanged.

### External MTP companion loading (2026-10-05, experimental and slower in smoke)

`--mtp-companion <directory>` with `--mtp-draft-tokens >0` loads a completed
local `mollm-mtp-weight-bundle-v1` alongside a target package. Packaged and
external MTP cannot be combined. The loader validates completion manifest,
context, graph, local paths, weight sizes/shapes/precision, listed references
and target HC width. Shared embedding/head constants borrow the target tensor
including its prepared device storage; target weight pointers are not replaced.
Dedicated constants use canonical absolute local paths, not target package refs.
CUDA companions do not build a second set of unused CPU FP16 expert sidecars;
canonical row-major mappings remain available for explicit fallback.

For existing Qwen4Exp packages, the loader recognizes the final GR_REDUCE,
GROUP_RMS_NORM and named target mixer gamma, and retains the exact preceding
GR_INJECT HC producer as an extra graph output. Only explicit companion loading
does this. No main weight bytes or graph arithmetic change, and normal logits
hidden stays last. Unknown mixer contracts/widths fail rather than guessing.
CPU and native-only CUDA synthetic runs cover ordinary and wide-state companion
drafts, retained-input verification, recurrent rejection/replay and repeated reset.
Negative tests cover size/context/path/precision/shape, unused manifest weights,
missing completion manifest and HC-width mismatch; failed loads allow engine reuse.

The first actual-model load caught a previously missed hard-coded W4 conversion
in the fused QKV exporter despite `_dense_precision="fp16"`. Both fused full and
linear attention exports now honor the option; default main export remains W4.

row order. Draft constant precision declarations now match FP16/FP32 output.

after validating unchanged weights, but cannot repair an incompatible weight file.

### Native CUDA FP16 MTP experts (2026-10-05)

CUDA now accepts canonical expert-major FP16 gate/up and down aggregates for
the single-group, shared-expert MoE contract used by the MTP draft. GPU routing,
weighted SwiGLU, shared expert and output combination reuse the existing native
pipeline. New FP16 projections accumulate in FP32; immutable GPU expert tables
are cached by prepared weight pointers and geometry. No NVFP4 layout change,
CPU fallback or second copy of the main experts is required.

Whole-MoE graph capture exposed a stream mismatch: cuBLAS handles defaulted to
the legacy stream even when our kernels compiled with per-thread default streams.
The backend now explicitly binds cuBLAS to `cudaStreamPerThread` in that build
configuration; legacy-default builds retain their existing behavior.

`test_cuda_fp16_moe` passes 35 projection cases (including partial rows/columns,
640/2560-wide inputs, output guards and nonblocking-stream graph replay) and 18
native-only MoE CPU comparisons across token counts, score functions and route
normalization. With per-thread streams, every MoE case also captures/replays the
whole operator twice with changed inputs, within absolute tolerance 2e-4.
All nine selected CUDA backend/MTP end-to-end CTests passed in 7.52 seconds.
These are correctness checks, not actual-model throughput or acceptance results.
Companion loading and existing target HC retention are now integrated above.

### MTP-only streamed FP16 export (2026-10-05, not loadable standalone)

`build_mtp_streamed_weights` resolves all26 dedicated weight references in
the actual Qwen3.8 MTP graph, excluding the shared target embedding/head.
It reuses the main mapping through a narrowly scoped MTP index adapter;
main-model export defaults are unchanged. Dense MTP projections stay FP16,
norms become FP32 effective Gemma gamma, and expert-major gate/up and down
aggregates are FP16 verification baselines, not additional low-bit quantization.

The source experts are E4M3FN with BF16 `weight_scale_inv` on128-by-128 blocks,
not the main model's NVFP4 format or the dense E8M0 format. The new decoder
handles BF16/F32 scales, partial row/column blocks and NaN/overflow checks.
Each transformed range covers at most128 rows; writes have no mutable row
counter and remain deterministic across writer chunk sizes. Tests cover
signed zero, FP8 subnormals/max finite values, both scale types,130-by-130 tails,
repeated chunk writes and distinctly signed expert/projection aggregation.

`tools/export_qwen4_mtp_weights.py` writes into a new/empty local directory,
never overwrites existing files, and emits the completion manifest last.
The real export is `/home/molly/workspace-mollm/qwen38-mtp-export.4OQh4z`:

`50a6523b57f426a91037549217e3287b2a20fe8e83ba423403b3b1b3398321b9`.
The original NFS model and existing main packages were not modified. This

### Qwen4Exp MTP graph builder (2026-10-05, export not yet integrated)

`models/qwen4_exp.py:build_mtp_graph` builds a dynamic single-full-attention
draft with shared embedding/head references, no PLE, separate `mtp_layers_0_*`
attention/MoE/hyper-connection references and its own MTP collapse mixer.
It keeps the wide state output separately from the final logits hidden.
The source config is deep-copied. Multiple draft layers, non-final target taps,
dedicated embeddings, non-full-attention drafts, HC count <=1 and differing
draft/target RoPE theta are rejected instead of silently changing semantics.

Input fusion globally normalizes the HC vector with effective Gemma gamma,
reshapes it into per-stream H-wide vectors, applies one shared H-by-H hidden
projection, and adds the projected normalized token embedding to every stream.
There is no expanded HC-by-HC matrix or replicated projection weight. This
matches the residual-linear-shared fusion described in the upstream SGLang
MTP implementation linked below. Export must add one to checkpoint norm gamma,
as the existing main-model export does.

Structural tests verify independent draft weights/caches, no target-layer or
PLE inputs, dynamic retained state, and preservation of target config. Twelve
NumPy graph-evaluation cases (H4/8, HC2/4/8, tokens1/3) match an independent
token-major formula, checking full-width normalization and stream/token layout.
This is not a CPU/CUDA kernel numeric test of the fusion or a weight-conversion
test. A read-only build against the actual local model config produces109 nodes,
10240-wide retained state,2560-wide logits hidden, one MoE and two2560-by-2560
input projections. Actual MTP weight export, package integration and model
acceptance/throughput validation remain incomplete; default inference is unchanged.

### Separate MTP residual state from logits hidden (2026-10-05)

Qwen4Exp graph construction now has an opt-in `export_mtp_state=True` argument.
It retains the pre-collapse hyperstream tensor as a graph output, identified
by graph metadata `mtp_state_output_node`, while the ordinary single-stream
logits hidden remains the final graph output. The package schema and weights
are unchanged. The converter does not enable this argument yet; existing
ordinary packages have no added state-copy operation or runtime transfer.

The engine captures declared target state for prefill, ordinary decode, and
speculative verification/replay; MTP draft recursion uses its own declared
state independently of the final hidden used for logits. Metadata must name
a retained graph output with FP32 [width, tokens, 1, 1] shape. Draft input width
is checked before execution to prevent reading a collapsed vector as a wider
state. Capture uses backend transfer hooks and remains host-backed for now.

This contract follows the two outputs in SGLang's
[Qwen4Exp MTP implementation](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen4_exp_mtp.py):
the logits processor receives the collapsed hidden, whereas draft recursion
receives the HC stream. The dedicated input projection applies its shared
H-to-H transform separately to each normalized stream.

The synthetic end-to-end fixture tests both the old 32-wide contract and a
128-wide retained-state/32-wide logits contract on CPU and native-only CUDA,
including a normal decode before eight speculative rejection steps and a
repeat after reset. Subsequent hidden states match retained-input references.
The Qwen4Exp structural test checks four-stream capture and preservation of
the final logits-output position. This is interface validation, not a completed
Qwen3.8 MTP export, acceptance/quality test, or throughput gain.

### Recurrent speculative-verification rollback (2026-10-05)

Speculative verification now checkpoints target GDN/conv, RWKV state/shift,
and plain auxiliary buffers through backend transfer hooks. On a rejected
draft or an early stop, it restores those buffers, rewinds KV lengths, and
replays only the retained inputs before synchronizing MTP. KV-only models
retain the existing length-only rollback. Ordinary generation does not enter
this path. No weight layout or conversion change is involved.

This is a correctness-first host snapshot, not an accelerated CUDA checkpoint:
GPU transfers and accepted-prefix replay have a cost. MTP statistics expose
cumulative checkpoint bytes, checkpoint time, rollback count, replay tokens,
and rollback time so that cost is not hidden. Unit coverage checks duplicate
states, failed captures, changed spans, accepted-only recurrent replay, opaque
device transfer hooks, and real CUDA persistent-buffer roundtrips.
`test_recurrent_mtp_e2e` additionally builds a synthetic Qwen3.5 GDN target
with native 128-wide recurrent heads and a deliberately poor cached-attention
draft. CPU and native-only CUDA each execute eight rejection steps, then
repeat after reset. Each run records eight recurrent rollbacks/eight replayed
tokens; subsequent hidden states are bit-identical to a non-speculative
retained-input prefill reference (not a serial-decode numeric-equivalence
claim). This is not a Qwen3.8 throughput result.
The current Qwen3.8 package still has no exported MTP graph; hyperstream-state
plumbing and its dedicated MTP weights remain to be implemented and verified.

The fixture exposed a writer bug: the package stores only MTP length, so the
loader expects its graph to end immediately at the weight offset. Alignment
padding was instead placed after the MTP graph, shifting the inferred start.
The writer now puts padding before MTP, with the same schema and unchanged
canonical weight payloads. Packages without MTP are byte-layout unaffected.
Malformed old MTP packages need rebuilding; the current non-MTP Qwen3.8
package does not. `test_mtp_package` checks graph magic at the inferred offset.

### CUDA W4 integer-MMA diagnostic (2026-10-05, not integrated)

`build_cuda/bench_cuda_q4_mma` is an independent W4/A8 prototype. It reads
the existing160-byte BG32 blocks, quantizes FP32 activation per32 values,
and applies the original per-row/group FP32 weight scales after each integer
dot product. No inference selector or package change was added.

The ordinary variant uses s8/s8 m16n8k32 MMA and activation codes[-127,127].
`MOLLM_Q4_DUAL_INT4=1` uses codes[-119,119], decomposed exactly into
`q = 16*high + low` with both signed4-bit parts, and two s4/s4 PTX MMA calls.
An exhaustive CPU check covers all239 codes. This preserves nearly8-bit
activation resolution, not a single4-bit quantizer; it still differs from
FP32-activation SIMT. On the current SM121 toolchain, disassembly shows S8
IMMA and extra conversion instructions for the s4 PTX path, not evidence
of native full-throughput INT4. Resources are31 registers for ordinary s8
and54 for dual4, zero stack/local usage; each uses3904 static shared bytes.

74 synthetic shape/input cases (rows1/3/16/19/64/65, K32/64/96/128/640/2560,
both variants plus zero input) at2/4/8 warps pass CPU integer-dot/double
references and output guards, including ragged output tiles. The first small
blocks have nonzero scales, avoiding a vacuous all-zero correctness gate.
`MOLLM_Q4_PREQUANT=1` quantizes once per call into a2560-byte buffer plus
320 scale bytes; the timer includes that extra kernel, not just projection.
The same numeric suite passes with prequantization enabled.

At N16480/K2560, eight rotating weight sets, ordinary s8 takes186.9–191.5 us
versus118.2–123.4 us SIMT (speedup0.629–0.651). Dual4 takes176.1–185.0 us
versus119.1–121.8 us (0.658–0.682). Quantizing once does not fix this:
s8 prequantized187.8–193.0 us and dual4 prequantized180.6–186.3 us.
All benchmark CPU-reference checks cover37 representative rows per weight
set; the small numeric suite checks every row. Against FP32 SIMT, the
synthetic relative-L2 differences are0.77% (s8) and1.15% (dual4), not a model
quality evaluation. These variants are slower and remain standalone only.

Logs: `build_cuda/q4-a8-mma-final-{,prequant-}validation.log`,
`build_cuda/q4-a8-{mma,dual4,prequant,dual4-prequant}-16480-1.log`,
`build_cuda/q4-a8-mma-{sass,resources}.log`. Standalone SM75 compilation
passes (MMA execution is skipped below SM80); no SM75 GPU runtime test was
performed.

### Qwen3.8 local MTP feasibility audit (2026-10-05, not implemented)

Read-only inspection of the original NFS config/index and safetensors headers
confirms one full-attention MTP layer,3101 indexed MTP tensors with payload
2516889600 expert bytes plus181136896 other bytes. The original shards were
not modified. Hyper-connection MTP parameters include a10240-element
`pre_fc_norm_hidden` and2560-by-2560 FC projections. The existing Qwen4
converter does not create an MTP graph; Qwen3-MoE conversion and the engine
already contain a single-head speculative framework, but cannot simply be
assumed compatible with these hyper-stream shapes.

The engine's current rejection path rewinds KV lengths only:
`speculative_decode` calls `set_cache_length`, whose implementation updates
only cache.k/cache.v metadata. Qwen4's GDN state/conv buffers are separately
allocated plain FP32 persistent tensors. Therefore a Qwen4 MTP implementation
must add and validate recurrent-state rollback, appropriate draft hidden
extraction, converter support and package/storage integration before testing
speedup. This is an identified next direction, not a working MTP capability
or an achieved model-performance improvement.

### CUDA W4 asynchronous weight staging prototype (2026-10-05, diagnostic only)

An experimental runtime selector tested a double-buffered four-group weight
stage only for N16480/K2560 canonical W4 decode projections. It copies whole
160-byte BG32 blocks through `cp.async` on SM80+ while computing the previous
four groups; SM75 uses a synchronous staging fallback. Accumulation and
reduction order are unchanged. Expert storage, precision and disk layout are
unchanged; per-CTA weight staging uses5120 bytes in addition to the existing
10240-byte activation cache. The option is not enabled by default.

`MOLLM_Q4_ASYNC_PROBE=1 build_cuda/bench_cuda_projections 16480 2560`
rotates eight weight sets (>128 MiB) and compares all outputs bit-exactly
against the current cached-wide four-group-prefetch control. Two independent
processes give speedups1.013/1.041/1.038 and1.029/1.034/1.009, candidate
114.815–118.484 us versus controls119.161–119.643 us. A CUDA regression
captures/replays twice on a nonblocking stream at rows1/19/31/33 and
K32/96/128/160/2560, testing partial staging groups, output guards and exact
results; the complete backend suite passes. Logs:
`build_cuda/q4-async-16480-{1,2}.log`, `build_cuda/q4-async-stream-regression.log`.
The same-build full-model SIMT control with warmup1/repeat4/max-new-tokens128
completed at `build_cuda/qwen38-q4-async-wide-control-repeat4.log`:127 decode
tokens in3392.39/3396.76/3391.44/3389.85 ms (37.39–37.46 tok/s).
The paired opt-in process completed at
`build_cuda/qwen38-q4-async-wide-repeat4.log`:decode3395.51/3394.78/3406.32/
3393.66 ms (37.28–37.42 tok/s), versus control mean3392.610 ms. Candidate
mean3397.568 ms is0.146% slower; all eight generated texts match. This
falsifies extrapolating the small rotating-pool gain to a model speedup.
The runtime `MOLLM_CUDA_Q4_ASYNC_WIDE` selector was removed; only the
standalone benchmark and correctness regression remain. Compilation reports
55 registers/6144 static shared bytes for async versus38 registers/1024
static shared bytes for the default kernel, both with zero stack/local usage.
Default resources remain the same as the previously linked chat binary.
After removing the runtime selector, bench/chat binaries were rebuilt and
the complete CUDA backend regression passes. A standalone SM75 compilation
of `matmul.cu` also passes after guarding the256B load hint (which requires
SM80+) with a128B fallback. This proves compilation, not runtime testing on
an SM75 GPU.

The preceding direct-load L2-size-hint diagnostic (64/128/256B, retaining
four-group prefetch) was bit-exact but steady-state speedups were about1.000.
An explicit no-hint PTX load control varied0.972–1.023, also not stable. That
path remains diagnostic only: `MOLLM_Q4_LOAD_HINT_PROBE=1`, log
`build_cuda/q4-load-hint-16480-1.log`. Hints follow
[NVIDIA's load-instruction documentation](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/parallel-thread-execution/index.html#data-movement-and-conversion-instructions-ld).

### CUDA W8 head CTA/shared-activation diagnostic (2026-10-05, not enabled)

`MOLLM_Q8_TUNING_PROBE=1 build_cuda/bench_cuda_projections --q8` compares

### CUDA canonical-weight prefill-only MMA prototype (2026-10-05)

`MOLLM_CUDA_NVFP4_MMA_PREFILL_ONLY=1` enables calibrated activation FP4
MMA only when the MoE input has more than one row. It accepts canonical
row/pair resident weights without requiring native-layout preparation or
another expert payload. Full-MMA and batched-N8 defaults remain unchanged;
canonical weights currently use the scalar MMA launcher, not N8 batching.
Decode retains the existing SIMT path. Checkpoint activation calibration is
still required; this is a precision-changing experimental mode, not a
bit-exact replacement for FP32-activation SIMT.

The reusable runtime kernel reads canonical fragments/scales directly.
88 synthetic cases covering row/pair layouts, gate/up globals, route output
weights and split-K1/2/4/8 match the native-layout MMA kernel bit for bit.
The standalone suite and complete CUDA backend regression pass. Full-model
warmup1/repeat2 completed at
`build_cuda/qwen38-canonical-mma-prefill-only-long.log`:365 prompt tokens,
prefill964.41/952.17 ms,31 decode tokens in827.06/827.66 ms. Relative to the
default sorted SIMT control1908.87/1905.22 ms, prefill throughput is1.990x;
decode timing is essentially unchanged. Native-layout full MMA remains faster
at744.89/743.41 ms prefill, so canonical access has a measurable cost.
Repeated greedy outputs are internally identical, but the hybrid text differs
from both the SIMT and full-MMA controls. This is not a model accuracy proof;
teacher-forced evaluation and an independent timing repeat remain required
before considering default promotion. No second resident expert copy exists.

Same-package teacher-forced prefill with chunk256,357 tokens/356 targets on
the self-authored bilingual fixture gives SIMT CE/PPL2.349851/10.484013 and
canonical MMA2.363291/10.625860 (+1.35% PPL). Native-layout MMA gives exactly
the same CE/PPL and an identical per-token-loss CSV as canonical MMA. Thus
this fixture does not show a canonical-reading regression, but activation
quantization is not lossless and the small fixture is not a quality benchmark.
Logs are `build_cuda/qwen38-prefill-{simt,hybrid,native-mma}-ppl.log`.

`mollm_ppl --decode-after-prefill 256` now scores the first256 tokens through
prefill and subsequent targets through single-token decode, retaining all
targets including the prefix/decode boundary. This is mutually exclusive
with `--decode-token-by-token`; ordinary chunked scoring is unchanged.
`test_ppl_decode_schedule` checks argument rejection, short/long prefixes,

The mixed-path SIMT control completed at
`build_cuda/qwen38-prefix256-simt-ppl.log`:256-token prefix then100 decode

2.348347/10.468256, finite logits,48 canonical-MMA calls (only the prefix).
The mixed-path fixture shows no PPL regression, unlike all-prefill scoring;

MMA modes remain experimental and off by default.
An independent warmup1/repeat4 hybrid timing process completed at

### CUDA compact W4 scale prototype (2026-10-05, not enabled)

`MOLLM_Q4_COMPACT_PROBE=1 build_cuda/bench_cuda_projections N K`
tests a private 144-byte BG32 block instead of the canonical 160-byte block.
Scales are encoded as BF16 maxima and reconstructed with FP32 division by
seven, not rounded to BF16 scales. Disk format and production dispatch remain
unchanged. Representative sequential GB10 microbenchmarks:

| N × K | Compact µs (three repeats) | Production control µs |
|---|---|---|
| 16480 × 2560 | 115.020 / 111.657 / 111.363 | 122.692 / 122.739 / 125.295 |
| 13312 × 2560 | 100.502 / 97.922 / 101.459 | 100.548 / 100.502 / 100.460 |
| 19 × 64 | 4.100 / 4.100 / 4.095 | 2.994 / 2.997 / 2.999 |

Output comparisons are bit-exact against the canonical wide kernel with the
same reduction tree, including ragged rows and zero scales. Small-shape
production dispatch uses a different reduction tree and is not bit-identical
to the wide kernel; its timing remains the control, not the equality reference.
The 16480-row result is promising, but the 13312-row result is inconsistent and
small shapes regress. No whole-model speedup or exhaustive scale-decoder
validation is claimed. CUDA backend regression tests passed after the change.

The shared mantissa table now uses exact integer rounding
`((128+m)*2^(m>=96?18:19)+3)/7`, eliminating its FP32 divisions.
All 128 mantissas match rounded FP32 division exactly. Rechecking 16480×2560
gave compact 115.124/112.739/111.151 µs versus control
123.566/123.890/125.963 µs, with bit-exact outputs. At 13312×2560,
101.305/101.318/99.887 µs versus 100.856/100.828/100.927 µs remains
essentially neutral. This change alone does not establish further acceleration.

The prototype additionally implements direct compact-to-FP16 prefill
preparation, without materializing canonical BG32 weights. The diagnostic
compares every expanded FP16 weight and the converted activation (including
an odd activation count) byte-for-byte with canonical preparation. Both
16480×2560 and ragged 19×64 pass. This bridge is still diagnostic-only; a
validated opt-in upload/dispatch integration and full-model comparison remain
required. After exercising the large preparation scratch, the three compact
decode timings were 117.395/118.637/118.687 µs against
122.973/122.880/122.921 µs, illustrating sensitivity to memory/cache conditions.

An experimental full-model integration is available through
`MOLLM_CUDA_Q4_COMPACT=1` (default off). It currently selects only
16480×2560 BG32 dense weights, validates every FP32 scale for bit-exact
reconstruction, and falls back to the canonical layout if any scale fails.
The sole device copy contains compact scales and biased nibbles; bounded
per-weight host staging is released after upload. Both decode GEMV and prefill
FP16 preparation consume this copy directly. Package format and CPU/Metal
representations are unchanged. Successful uploads report saved bytes.
The first calibrated-package SIMT whole-model run
(`build_cuda/qwen38-compact-wide-simt.log`, warmup 1, repeat 2) compressed 36
weights and saved 94,924,800 device bytes (90.53 MiB). Both runs generated
174 tokens/173 decode tokens with text identical to both historical canonical
SIMT runs; internal repeat validation also checks token IDs and EOS.
Decode took 4610.01/4603.86 ms (37.53/37.58 tok/s), and 24-token prefill
took 205.21/206.11 ms. The historical canonical decode was 37.30/37.29
tok/s, but a fresh same-build canonical control is still pending; no confirmed
end-to-end speedup is claimed from that historical comparison.

The fresh same-build canonical control completed with decode
4648.09/4675.89 ms (37.22/37.00 tok/s), prefill 205.21/204.71 ms,
and text identical across both control and compact repeats. The mean decode
time reduction is 1.18% for this single process pair; further independent
pairs are required before calling it a stable improvement.

A compact narrow-projection diagnostic preserves the original 256-thread
reduction tree and passes bit-exact decode and FP16-preparation checks at
2560×6144. It regresses: integer scale restoration gives
70.643/66.866/66.717 µs versus 59.620/60.573/58.931 µs. A shared mantissa
table makes it worse (73.776/70.313/70.406 versus 59.110/59.053/59.052 µs)
and was removed. Narrow compact dispatch remains diagnostic-only and is
not selected by the opt-in full-model uploader. Saving 10% of weight bytes
does not by itself outweigh scale restoration and access-pattern costs.

The independent true-N8 MMA prototype now computes eight distinct tokens
against one expert's native weight/scales in a single operation. Descriptors
in each fixed group of eight must share weight, block-scale and row-scale
pointers; input globals, up globals and output route weights may differ.
Every B column has its own FP4 activation/FP8 scales and all four accumulator
registers are scattered to the appropriate two output columns and two rows.
It does not modify the existing scalar kernel or production dispatch.

`bench_cuda_nvfp4_mma` validates this reusable launcher for rows 16/48/128,
K64/640/2560, both source layouts and split64 gate/up globals. Eight different
inputs/calibrations and signed/zero route weights match eight individual
native projections byte-for-byte (`build_cuda/nvfp4-batched8-validation.log`).
This establishes fragment correctness only: variable-size expert grouping,
padding/packing, realistic timing and model integration remain to be done.

The variable-size grouped launcher now generates GPU batch metadata for
adjacent descriptors sharing all three expert weight/scale pointers, splits
each run into at most eight tokens, and masks tail-column stores. Tail
columns duplicate the final valid input only for MMA padding; no invalid
descriptor or output is accessed. A stream-ordered memset plus linear-run
builder avoids races between initialization and sparse metadata writes.
Scratch is eight bytes per route, with no extra weight copies or host routing.

The reusable probe tests counts 1/3/7/8/9/17 across two experts, including
a nine-token run, reversed output destinations and untouched inactive
destinations. Rows16/48/128, K64/640/2560, both source layouts and gate/up
split64 remain byte-exact against separate native projections
(`build_cuda/nvfp4-grouped8-validation.log`). Sparse CTA dispatch and padded
quantization are still unmeasured; production integration is not enabled.

`MOLLM_NVFP4_GROUPED_BENCH=1 MOLLM_NVFP4_PROBE_DEVICE_POOL=1
bench_cuda_nvfp4_mma` now measures real gate/up1280×2560 and down2560×640
with ten synthetic experts, 1/2/4/8 distinct tokens per expert, cycling
at least 128 MiB of private CUDA weights across sets. Every set is checked
byte-for-byte; timers include batch initialization and grouping. The initial
implementation was slower: gate singletons ~121 µs versus ~87 µs scalar,
and eight-token groups ~122–127 µs versus ~118–125 µs. Down groups also
regress. These results do not support model integration.

Tail columns now receive zero packed values/scales instead of re-quantizing
the final input. Gate singletons fall to 92.380/92.638/92.407 µs versus
87.719/88.811/86.103 µs; two-token groups ~97.3–97.6 versus ~89.8–92.5 µs;
four-token groups ~105–108 versus ~104–107 µs; full groups remain near
124–126 versus ~122–126 µs. Results and exact-output checks are in
`build_cuda/nvfp4-grouped-real-shape-zero-padding.log`. Redundant activation
quantization across output row tiles remains a concrete implementation cost
to remove; reducing MMA instruction count alone has not improved these timings.

The grouped API now optionally accepts packed-activation and FP8-scale
scratch, quantizes each route once (two distinct globals for gate/up), and
loads the prepared B fragments directly in the MMA kernel. This removes
per-output-tile quantization and shared-activation staging. It retains exact
FP32 global/route postscaling and masked ragged output stores. Scratch holds
`count*(split_row?2:1)*K/2` packed bytes plus `/16` FP8 scale bytes.
All existing two-expert/ragged/reversed-scatter counts pass byte-exact
comparison with individual projections, including both gate/up globals
(`build_cuda/nvfp4-grouped-prequant-validation.log`).

Adding `MOLLM_NVFP4_GROUPED_PREQUANT=1` to the real-shape device-pool probe
includes quantization, grouping and compute in its timer. Gate/up four-token
groups: 94.649/94.804/94.805 µs versus scalar 106.009/109.149/107.988 µs;
eight-token groups: 98.870/99.105/99.005 versus 125.132/125.063/125.541 µs.
Singletons and two-token groups do not benefit. Down eight-token groups:
54.265/50.563/54.290 versus 59.740/59.677/59.702 µs; smaller groups do
not consistently benefit (`build_cuda/nvfp4-grouped-real-shape-prequant.log`).
These are synthetic projection gains, not whole-model gains. An adaptive
group-size policy, routed sorting cost and actual prefill distributions must
be verified before default integration; decode dispatch remains unchanged.

Grouped MMA now supports `min_batch_size` 1–8. Metadata records each route's
chunk size; large chunks use N8, small chunks use a separately specialized
filtered scalar kernel. Prequantization skips small chunks. The existing
default scalar kernel is an unfiltered specialization, not a new runtime
branch. Thresholds1/4/8 pass all prior ragged/two-expert/reverse-scatter
checks, with prepared scratch poisoned before each test to detect accidental
reads from skipped groups (`build_cuda/nvfp4-grouped-adaptive-validation.log`).

`MOLLM_NVFP4_GROUPED_ADAPTIVE=1` selects gate threshold4/down threshold8 in
the real-shape probe. Gate four-token groups measure 93.668/96.738/98.815 µs
versus 105.347/105.276/105.225 µs; eight-token groups 103.546/103.610/103.722
versus 120.832/121.013/123.042 µs. Singleton/two-token cases still regress
from launch/metadata overhead; down eight-token groups have only a small
gain (54.195/56.133/57.397 versus 56.472/56.952/59.462 µs). Thus adaptive
expert thresholds alone are insufficient: a prefill batch-size gate and
real routing distribution/sorting timings are required. No model path is
enabled by these diagnostics (`build_cuda/nvfp4-grouped-real-shape-adaptive.log`).

`MOLLM_CUDA_NVFP4_MMA_PREFILL_BATCH=1` adds an experimental model integration,
default off. It requires native calibrated MMA, parts=1, at least128 prefill
tokens, enabled expert grouping and at most4096 routes. Only this opt-in
extends the existing stable rank-sort from2048 to4096 routes; its sorting
cost is included in model timings. Gate/up threshold4 and down threshold8
select hybrid grouped projections; smaller chunks retain individual MMA.
Decode and short-prefill dispatch are unchanged. A single reusable scratch
allocation holds batch metadata plus packed activations/scales, reused
between gate/up and down; no resident weight duplicate is created.
The backend reports batch-call count and scratch capacity at teardown.

CUDA regression tests pass with the flag. Full-model validation is running
against `tests/data/qwen38_nvfp4_sanity.txt`, warmup1/repeat2/max-new-tokens32,
at `build_cuda/qwen38-native-mma-batched-prefill-long.log`. Actual activation,
deterministic output comparison and same-build unbatched control are pending;
no whole-model gain is claimed yet.

The first long-prompt batched model run completed: 365 prompt tokens,
prefill717.11/714.05 ms (508.99/511.17 tok/s), 32 generated/31 decode
tokens, decode846.61/847.31 ms. Internal two-repeat token/text/EOS checks
pass. Teardown confirms144 batched MoE calls and8,388,608 scratch bytes,
so the path actually executed. Same-build unbatched control is running at
`build_cuda/qwen38-native-mma-batched-prefill-long-control.log`.
Because the opt-in also admits256-token batches to sorting, a sort-only
ablation is needed to distinguish weight-locality gains from true-N8 gains.

The unbatched control completed with prefill1427.49/1429.54 ms
